newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bourses to launch options on stocks in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan bourses to launch options on stocks in July.

text.p: Japan's two biggest bourses announced on Tuesday that they would offer options on individual stocks for the first time in July.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) and the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE) both said they would launch the new options trade on July 18.

Compared with other major financial centres, Japan has been cautious about derivative products. It introduced stock index options in the 1980s but has held back from launching options on specific shares until now.
The Tokyo bourse said in a statement it would select stocks for options trade from among issues whose average monthly trade volume has exceeded three million shares for the past year.
To qualify, the firms must also must have more than 130 million shares outstanding and have over 5,000 shareholders at the end of their latest business year, the TSE said.
The OSE said it would select stocks included in both the Nikkei 225 and Nikkei 300 indices, based on how international they are and what industries they represent.
"At first only a few issues will be offered, but the number will be increased depending on how well they do," OSE president Kyoji Kitamura told reporters.
He said the selection would be made next month.
Both bourses said their minimum transaction fee would be 2,500 yen ($19).
The TSE said the fee for trades of more than five million yen ($39,600) would be 0.6 percent of the total trade.

The TSE also unveiled on Tuesday a plan to allow trading from June 1 of depositary receipts, or receipts for shares, issued in overseas markets by foreign firms. The move is designed to make it easier for foreign firms, especially in Asia, to raise funds.

Such instruments are known as ADRs (American depositary receipts) in the United States, where investors can buy them instead of buying shares of foreign-based companies. The holder is entitled to dividends and capital gains but has no voting rights. ($1=126 yen)
